classification.difficultyReason: Select supplied descriptions by reading direction and changing steepness. The hardest distinction is that a descending curve can show increasing speed when its negative gradient becomes steeper; this directly applies the taught rules.

inlines.text: For each graph, select an appropriate description from the list given.

answer.short: Distance: not changing. Gradient: zero. Speed: zero and constant.
answer.worked: The horizontal line shows that distance does not change. Its gradient is zero, so the object is stopped. Its speed is zero throughout and is therefore also constant.

answer.short: Distance: decreasing. Gradient: negative. Speed: constant.
answer.worked: The line slopes downwards, so distance decreases and the gradient is negative. It is straight, so its steepness and the speed remain constant.

answer.short: Distance: increasing. Gradient: positive. Speed: increasing.
answer.worked: The curve rises, so distance increases and the gradient is positive. It becomes steeper, so speed increases.

answer.short: Distance: increasing. Gradient: positive. Speed: decreasing.
answer.worked: The curve rises, so distance increases and the gradient is positive. It becomes less steep, so speed decreases.

answer.short: Distance: decreasing. Gradient: negative. Speed: decreasing.
answer.worked: The curve falls, so distance decreases and the gradient is negative. It becomes less steep, so speed decreases.

answer.short: Distance: decreasing. Gradient: negative. Speed: increasing.
answer.worked: The curve falls, so distance decreases and the gradient is negative. It becomes steeper downwards, so speed increases.

inlines.text: The direction of the graph gives the sign of the gradient. Speed is the magnitude of that gradient: increasing steepness means increasing speed; a horizontal segment has zero, constant speed.
